=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:118-123 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The no-recommendation block's trigger (line 118) and headline (line 121) blame only merge conflicts, although step 6 line 42 now also routes to it when every candidate is blocked on an unshipped prerequisite. The mirror workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md has the same text.
  WHY: The header names the wrong cause, and the re-run line points at the wrong unblock event (merging PRs instead of the prerequisite shipping). All reviewers rated this NIT.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:42 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The closing sentence "If no candidate qualifies, the recommendation stays the single anchor plan." can be read as covering a failed anchor prerequisite. That reading contradicts the earlier rule that the anchor is "not recommended, alone or bundled".
  WHY: A model could recommend a non-startable anchor. Severity disagreement: minimax_minimax-m3 rated MAJOR, and the other two rated NIT.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:105-110 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The text requires dependency order, with a prerequisite member listed ahead of the anchor. The example template always lists the anchor first and the member second.
  WHY: Copying the example puts the anchor ahead of its own prerequisite, which reverses the required Hand off order. Severity disagreement: minimax_minimax-m3 rated MAJOR, and openai_gpt-6-luna rated NIT.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:87-88 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The new "Blocked on an unshipped prerequisite" row reads "(<in flight in issue #N / screened out / over the bundle caps>)". It drops the "orchestrator" qualifier used on adjacent rows, and its "screened out" case has no slot for the blocking issue/PR or the overlapping paths.
  WHY: The row is inconsistent with lines 82 and 85 and with the line 36 evidence-based screening rule, so the report loses traceability. All reviewers rated this NIT.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: The PR description says 5 contract tests pin the bundle rules. The last run added the anchor-prerequisite fallback, the "Blocked on an unshipped prerequisite" section, the no-recommendation alternative wording, and the "prerequisite of the anchor goes ahead of the anchor" ordering.
  expected_change_site: tests/test_audit_plans_command.py (test_bundle_requires_relatedness_and_caps, test_bundle_output_names_a_single_hand_off, test_bundle_rule_lives_in_the_gate_after_the_pick)
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: tests/test_audit_plans_command.py has no assertions for "the anchor is not startable now and is not recommended, alone or bundled", "Blocked on an unshipped prerequisite (only if any):", "(or: blocked on unshipped prerequisite <plan>)", or "a member that is a prerequisite of the anchor goes ahead of the anchor". A later edit could drop these rules without failing CI. Both reviewers rated this NIT. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 calls it hardening of the PR's own coverage, and no linked issue exists.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:118,121 (mirror: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The no-recommendation block's trigger and header blame only merge conflicts, although step 6 line 42 now also routes there when the anchor is blocked on an unshipped prerequisite and no next-ranked candidate remains.
  WHY: The header is wrong for the prerequisite case, and the re-run line points at the wrong unblock event.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:42 (mirror: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: "If no candidate qualifies, the recommendation stays the single anchor plan." could cover the anchor's own prerequisite failure. The intended reading is that no member candidate qualifies to join a bundle.
  WHY: A model could still recommend a non-startable anchor. The risk is low because the earlier sentence is explicit.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md: new "Blocked on an unshipped prerequisite (only if any):" Output Format block (mirror: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The "screened out" case cites neither the blocking issue/PR nor the paths, unlike the "Conflict-screened out" block.
  WHY: This is a wording inconsistency only. It leaves the "screening is evidence-based" rule applied unevenly.
- TASK_GAP: tests/test_audit_plans_command.py | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  Requirement: The PR description says 5 contract tests pin the bundle rules. The last run added behavior that is not pinned: the anchor-prerequisite fallback, the "Blocked on an unshipped prerequisite" section, the no-recommendation alternative wording, and the "prerequisite of the anchor goes ahead of the anchor" ordering.
  Expected change site: tests/test_audit_plans_command.py, in test_bundle_requires_relatedness_and_caps or test_bundle_output_names_a_single_hand_off.
  Evidence of absence: The test diff has no assertion for "the anchor is not startable now and is not recommended, alone or bundled", "Blocked on an unshipped prerequisite (only if any):", or "a member that is a prerequisite of the anchor goes ahead of the anchor".
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: tests/test_audit_plans_command.py, test_bundle_requires_relatedness_and_caps. Add assertions for "the anchor is not startable now and is not recommended, alone or bundled" in step6 and "Blocked on an unshipped prerequisite (only if any):" in text. About 2 lines changed. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:42 (and mirror workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md:42) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The trailing sentence "If no candidate qualifies, the recommendation stays the single anchor plan" sits in the same paragraph as the rule that forbids recommending an anchor with a failed prerequisite, alone or bundled. It could be applied to the failed-anchor case.
  WHY: An LLM could pick the anchor anyway and start a project whose phases depend on a plan that does not yet exist.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:105 vs lines 107-115 (and mirror) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The leading sentence requires dependency order, with a prerequisite member ahead of the anchor. The example always shows the anchor first and the member second.
  WHY: Copying the example puts the anchor ahead of its own prerequisite, so the Hand off paths are out of dependency order and the dispatch order is reversed.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:118-124 (and mirror) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Step 6 now reaches the no-recommendation outcome by two paths, conflicts and prerequisite blocks. The trigger and headline describe only the merge-conflict path, and the closing sentence tells the user to wait for blocking PRs to merge.
  WHY: The unblock event named in the closing line is wrong when the cause is a prerequisite block.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:87-88 (and mirror) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The parenthetical has three branches ("in flight", "screened out", "over the bundle caps"), but only "in flight" carries an issue number. The "screened out" branch has no slot for the paths or the blocking issue/PR required by line 36 and the line-85 template.
  WHY: The audit's evidence-based rule (line 146) is silently skipped for this row, and the screened-out prerequisite block cannot be traced.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:88 (and mirror) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: "in flight in issue #N" drops the "orchestrator" qualifier that lines 82 and 85 use.
  WHY: The report template is inconsistent across rows, and downstream parsing of the parenthetical needs special-casing.
- TASK_GAP: tests/test_audit_plans_command.py | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  Requirement: The PR description lists 5 contract tests pinning the bundle rules. The last run's diff added new step-6 wording that the existing tests do not pin.
  Expected change site: tests/test_audit_plans_command.py, in test_bundle_rule_lives_in_the_gate_after_the_pick, test_bundle_requires_relatedness_and_caps and test_bundle_output_names_a_single_hand_off.
  Evidence of absence: The test file has no assertions for "the anchor is not startable now and is not recommended, alone or bundled", "The anchor's own declared prerequisites follow the same rule", "Blocked on an unshipped prerequisite (only if any):", "(or: blocked on unshipped prerequisite <plan>)", or "a member that is a prerequisite of the anchor goes ahead of the anchor".
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: NONE
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:42,118-123 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The prerequisite-blocking path can produce "no recommendation", but the template says this happens because every viable plan risks merge conflicts. The rerun instruction mentions only merges or project completion.
  WHY: The report gives the wrong reason and does not name the prerequisite shipping as the event to wait for.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:105,108-110 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The instructions require dependency order, with a prerequisite of the anchor first, but the example always lists the anchor before the member.
  WHY: Following the example puts the plans in the opposite of the required dependency order.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: tests/test_audit_plans_command.py, test_bundle_rule_lives_in_the_gate_after_the_pick and test_bundle_output_names_a_single_hand_off. Add assertions for the "not startable now" clause and the "Blocked on an unshipped prerequisite" output heading. About 2 lines changed. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:118,121-123 (mirror: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md), interacting with line 42 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The last run added a second route into the no-recommendation block, plus the bullet alternative "(or: blocked on unshipped prerequisite <plan>)". The trigger (line 118) and headline (line 121) still state only the merge-conflict cause.
  WHY: An audit where all candidates are prerequisite-blocked prints a false cause and a re-run instruction (line 123) pointing at the wrong unblock event. The same header ships to consumer repos via the template copy.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:42 (mirror: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The closing sentence "If no candidate qualifies, the recommendation stays the single anchor plan." can be read as covering the anchor itself. That contradicts the earlier rule that a blocked anchor "is not startable now and is not recommended, alone or bundled."
  WHY: Under the broad reading, a run could recommend the single blocked anchor and dispatch a project built on unshipped prerequisite code.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:88 (mirror: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The new template line diverges from the "orchestrator issue #N" convention of lines 82 and 85. Its "screened out" alternative omits the blocking issue/PR and overlapping paths required by line 36 and the line-85 row.
  WH
